topics.label: Course Introduction and Lecture Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening section introduces the structure and scope of the cancer biology lecture series and outlines the specific learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cellular, Genetic, and Experimental Foundations of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer arises through accumulated genetic changes and disrupted cellular differentiation, along with the laboratory methods used to examine these cellular behaviors.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Stepwise Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the histological and clinical distinctions between benign and malignant lesions through the mechanisms of tissue invasion, metastatic dissemination, and colorectal tumor progression.

topics.label: Principles of Tumor Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard conventions and notable exceptions for classifying and naming benign and malignant neoplasms based on their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physiological and anatomical mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors disrupt organ function and cause patient death.

topics.label: Comparative Epidemiology and Cross-Species Incidence of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of cancer incidence and tissue susceptibility in humans as well as across diverse multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Clinical Detection and Cancer Screening Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss early clinical presentation and evaluate the diagnostic principles, benefits, and limitations of population screening across major cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic reiterates the core learning outcomes and wraps up the lecture.
